NoteNlpAccessor::align_tokens¶

Back to Note NLP Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

TokenBatch NoteNlpAccessor::align_tokens(const Note& other) const

Word-Level Alignment Of Two Notes¶

align_tokens(other) compares each cell of self against the matching cell of other one word at a time and returns the full alignment as a TokenBatch of tag-prefixed tokens. It is the word-granularity member of the diff / align family — the counterpart of align_sentences, and the equal-included sibling of diff_words.

How the comparison works¶

Each cell pair is first tokenized into words with the same tokenizer as tokens: a word is a run of ASCII letters and digits (with _, interior single -/', trailing +/#, and recognized URLs / emails / dotted abbreviations kept whole). Everything between words — spaces and standalone punctuation — is dropped before the comparison, so align_tokens never reports a punctuation-only edit; "stop here" and "stop, here!" align as two = tokens.

The two word lists are aligned by their longest common subsequence and every word is emitted once, in order, with a one-byte tag:

Tag

Meaning

In self

In other

=

unchanged — part of the common subsequence

yes

yes

-

removed — in self, not matched in other

yes

no

+

added — in other, not matched in self

no

yes

The tag is the first character of the token; the word follows immediately. Keeping the = tokens makes each cell’s stream a full transcript that rebuilds other from self. For the change-only view, use diff_words — it runs the same alignment and omits the = tokens.

The TokenBatch result¶

Tags from all cells are concatenated into one rank-1 token Note, batch.tokens(). The rank-1 Int64 Note batch.offsets() has length numel + 1 and marks each cell’s run. Cell r owns tokens.at(k) for k in [offsets[r], offsets[r + 1]). Identical cells contribute a run of = tokens, one per word.

Shape, pairing, and rejections¶

Comparison is per cell and pairwise. self and other must share the same numel, or one may be a scalar (numel() == 1) broadcast against every cell of the other. Rejections raise pluss::Error:

  • bytes-mode self → NoteNlpAccessor::align_tokens requires a UTF-8 text Note (lhs is bytes).

  • unequal numel, neither side scalar → NoteNlpAccessor::align_tokens expects equal numel or scalar broadcast.

The alignment is O(m · n) in words per cell and deterministic: on a tie the - (removal) is emitted before the + (insertion).

Example 1: One Word Substituted¶

const auto batch = pluss::make_note({"the quick brown fox"})
                       .nlp().align_tokens(pluss::make_note({"the slow brown fox"}));

std::cout << pluss::note::print(batch.tokens()) << "\n";
std::cout << "offsets: [";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < batch.offsets().integers().size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << batch.offsets().integers()[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[5], dim=1, numel=5, encoding=utf8)
["=the", "-quick", "+slow", "=brown", "=fox"]
offsets: [0, 5]

the, brown, and fox are shared. quick is replaced by slow, which shows as the adjacent -quick / +slow pair.

Example 2: Identical Cells Are All =¶

const auto batch = pluss::make_note({"same words"})
                       .nlp().align_tokens(pluss::make_note({"same words"}));
std::cout << pluss::note::print(batch.tokens()) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["=same", "=words"]

Example 3: Per-Cell Runs¶

const auto batch = pluss::make_note({"a b c", "x y"})
                       .nlp().align_tokens(pluss::make_note({"a c", "x z"}));

std::cout << pluss::note::print(batch.tokens()) << "\n";
std::cout << "offsets: [";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < batch.offsets().integers().size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << batch.offsets().integers()[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[6], dim=1, numel=6, encoding=utf8)
["=a", "-b", "=c", "=x", "-y", "+z"]
offsets: [0, 3, 6]

Cell 0’s alignment is tokens()[0..3) (b deleted); cell 1’s is tokens()[3..6) (y replaced by z).
